You are an experienced NSW HSC Modern History marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC Modern History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting. Judge the response the way HSC Modern History markers do: a direct answer to the question, a sustained judgement where the directive verb asks for one, specific and accurate evidence (dates, names, cases, legislation, sources, historians) and the terms of the course. Do not reward length or narrative for its own sake.

Question 19(c) [12 marks]: How successful were Deng Xiaoping’s reforms in China?

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
11–12 marks: Makes an insightful and sustained judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses detailed, specific, relevant and accurate historical information to support their judgement | Communicates ideas in a logical and well-structured form which uses a range of relevant historical terms and concepts appropriately
9–10 marks: Makes a well-reasoned judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses relevant and accurate historical information to support their judgement | Communicates ideas in a logical and structured form using relevant historical terms and concepts appropriately
6–8 marks: Makes a judgement about the success of the relevant feature | Uses relevant and accurate historical information | Communicates ideas in a logical and structured form using some historical terms and concepts
3–5 marks: Provides a description about the relevant feature | Uses some relevant historical detail including terms and concepts in their response
1–2 marks: Provides some relevant historical information

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Deng Xiaoping's economic reforms, initiated in the late 1970s, transformed China from a centrally planned, stagnating economy into one of the world's most dynamic and powerful economic forces making them extremely successful. Deng's pragmatic approach marked a departure from strict communist ideologies, focusing on economic pragmatism and modernisation. The success of his reforms was due to economic growth, social changes, and the global positioning of China during this period.

ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
• Introduction of market-based economy and foreign investment
• Creation of Special Economic Zones
• Household Responsibility System replacing collective farming contributed to productivity
• Emphasis on science and technology allowed China to emerge as a leader in various industries, including manufacturing, telecommunications, and information technology
• Open-door policy fostered growth
• One child policy focused resources on economy.



STUDENT RESPONSE:
